exposure: IOL at 39 weeks vs expectant management at 39 weeks
IOL at 40 weeks vs expectant management at 40 weeks
IOL at 38 weeks vs expectant management at 38 weeks
IOL at 37 weeks vs expectant management at 37 weeks
cohort: Obese women (BMI ≥ 35) with term, singleton, vertex deliveries at the Townsville Hospital and Health Service from January 2011 to June 2015
finding: In women with a BMI ≥ 35, IOL does not affect the CS rate, or the risk of neonatal adverse events, but may increase the rate of postpartum haemorrhage when compared with expectant management.
mod_finding: In women with a BMI ≥ 35, induction of labor at term did not affect the cesarean section rate or neonatal adverse events compared to expectant management.
